extracted.intended_audience: defense contractors, industry stakeholders, government procurement professionals, small businesses, and members of the public who submit comments on DFARS rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submittingwritten public comments on proposed DFARS (Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement) rules, including submission mechanics, communication channels, and the substantive content and evidence that make comments effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on proposed rules should be submitted in writing to the address shown in the Federal Register notice on or before the specified comment deadline. Comments should be submitted identified by the specific DFARS Case number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you use the mailing or submission address in the specific Federal Register notice, meet the deadline, and include the DFARS case number so the comment is associated with the correct rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum public comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD generally requires proposed rules to provide not less than a 30-day public comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan to submit within the stated window; if less than 30 days is provided, note that the department's general practice is a minimum 30-day period (useful when evaluating timeliness or procedural adequacy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use web-based email for questions and comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Web-based email account for the public and industry officials to ask questions, recommend changes, or comment on DFARS rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the Federal Register notice provides a web-based email address and use it for clarifying questions or to submit comments where permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participate via Advanced Notices of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced Notices of Proposed Rulemaking used to receive early public input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage early when ANPRMs are published to shape rule development before formal proposed rules are issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and contact DOD points of contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying DOD points of contacts in Federal Register notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the listed points of contact to direct questions, seek clarification of scope, or request meetings when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend or engage in public meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Public meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When public meetings are offered, attend to provide oral input, clarify written submissions, and hear agency perspectives and stakeholder concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific DFARS sections and subsections
rubrics_metrics.description: For defense acquisition rules, effective comments: Cite specific DFARS sections and subsections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point reviewers to exact regulatory text you are addressing (section and subsection) rather than only describing issues in general terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference FAR parallel provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) parallel provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the proposed DFARS language compares to FAR provisions, including relevance or conflicts, to help reviewers assess consistency with existing procurement rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address contractor implementation costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Address contractor implementation costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include estimates or data on the costs contractors will incur to comply with the proposed requirement (one-time and recurring), and explain methodological assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish small business and large prime contractor impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish small business and large prime contractor impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss differential burdens, compliance capabilities, and impacts on competition for small vs. large firms; provide data if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with security clearance and CMMC requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with security clearance and CMMC requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the proposed rule interacts with security clearance processes or Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) obligations, and identify operational difficulties or redundancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite Defense Science Board, NIST, and other technical guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite Defense Science Board, NIST, and other technical guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support technical claims with references to relevant authoritative technical guidance or standards to bolster credibility and specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address supply chain risk management dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Address supply chain risk management dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify how proposed requirements affect supply chain risk assessments, visibility, traceability, resiliency, and mitigation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference international supplier impacts (CFIUS, TAA, BAA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference international supplier impacts (CFIUS, TAA, BAA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss implications for foreign suppliers, cross-border transactions, and compliance with Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS), Trade Agreements Act (TAA), Buy American Act (BAA), or related rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address cybersecurity and IP protection requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with cybersecurity and IP protection requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the rule will affect cybersecurity practices and intellectual property protection, including potential conflicts and implementation challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide cost data on compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide cost data on compliance with new requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit quantitative cost data, including estimates, assumptions, and sources. Concrete numbers strengthen rulemaking comments and support regulatory impact analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Buy American Act implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Address Buy American Act implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify whether the proposal interacts with domestic sourcing statutes and how it may affect domestic vs. foreign sourcing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common DFARS Topics for Comment: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When CMMC is implicated, provide detailed feedback on scope, levels, assessment approaches, timelines, and industry readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on sourcing restrictions (Section 889)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common DFARS Topics for Comment: Sourcing restrictions (Section 889 prohibitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address operational impacts, compliance verification, supplier identification, and mitigation strategies for Section 889 restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on cost accounting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Common DFARS Topics for Comment: Cost accounting standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss accounting and allocation burdens, compliance costs, and how standards would be implemented by contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on audit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Common DFARS Topics for Comment: Audit requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide input on scope, frequency, cost, and administrative burden of proposed audit provisions and suggested alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on conflict mineral disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Common DFARS Topics for Comment: Conflict mineral disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe supplier reporting burdens, traceability challenges, and potential effects on sourcing and supply chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on anti-counterfeit electronic part requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Common DFARS Topics for Comment: Anti-counterfeit electronic part requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence or examples of counterfeit risks, mitigation practices, testing approaches, and cost impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on past performance reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Common DFARS Topics for Comment: Past performance reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer feedback on reporting metrics, data collection burdens, relevance to award decisions, and privacy or proprietary data concerns.
